notes: The five DPR 523D district records published with the South of Market Area Historic Resource Survey (2007-2010; HPC Resolution No. 103, 16 February 2011), listed on the archived Planning page https://sfgov.org/sfplanningarchive/south-market-area-historic-resource-survey and fetched plainly from default.sfplanning.org/GIS/SouthSoMa/Docs/: Sixth Street Lodginghouse (Anne Bloomfield 1997, transcribed by N. Moses Corrette 2010, 5 pp.), Bluxome and Townsend Warehouse (Christina Dikas, Page & Turnbull, June 2009, 21 pp.), South End Historic District Addition (Dikas, June 2009, 26 pp.), South Park (Dikas, 30 June 2009, 47 pp.) and Western SoMa Light Industrial and Residential (Dikas and Corrette, March 2009 / October 2010, 124 pp.). Extracted: historic building names, per-building construction, architect, builder and developer credits, original and long-running business occupants, sales, and the other works with street numbers that the architects' biographies name. Not extracted: contributor status and ratings (the soma-survey batch published them from the results table, and Western SoMa's 721-row element table is that same table); private residents named from city directories and the census; owners from chain-of-title research; the pre-1906 South Park residents, whose houses all burned in 1906.

coverage.remaining: Nothing of these five records. Two things in them were deliberately left: the pre-1906 South Park residents table (Shumate's 1856-1885 list, 100+ heads of household with numbers on houses destroyed in 1906; candidates for the South Park place page's timeline, not for any standing building) and the Western SoMa element table's descriptive site notes (e.g. 3727001, the Flamingo Motel's Best Western role), which the soma-survey batch counted but did not publish.
coverage.note: All 223 PDF pages read: narrative, contributor lists and architect biographies. 219 findings: 31 Sixth Street, 20 Bluxome and Townsend, 34 South End Addition, 38 South Park, 96 Western SoMa, 52 of them from its designer lists. Across all five, 42 findings come from architects' biographies naming works outside the districts. 190 resolved, 29 unresolved (addresses with no EAS record, ranges now split across parcels, condominium parcels, and 96 Sixth, whose printed lot is on the other side of the street). 124 published on 106 pages, 13 of them seeded; 66 declined, 57 of them because the page already carried the fact — the South of Market context statement reprints most of these records' designer lists — 6 because the roll dates the parcel's building decades after the fact, and 3 hotel names the page could not take as given.
